writtenTo: Those searching for meaning and purpose in life
importantNotes: 'Vanity of vanities' (1:2) — the Hebrew word 'hevel' means breath, vapor, or fleeting.
The book is not pessimistic — it's realistic about life apart from God.
Ecclesiastes 3:1-8 ('a time for everything') is one of the most quoted passages in literature.
The conclusion (12:13) is the key: 'Fear God and keep his commandments.'
Solomon had experienced everything — wealth, pleasure, power — and found it all empty without God.

chapters.1: 'Vanity of vanities' — everything is meaningless; there is nothing new under the sun.
chapters.2: The Teacher tests pleasure, projects, and wealth — all is vanity and chasing after wind.
chapters.3: A time for everything; God has set eternity in the human heart.
chapters.4: The injustice of oppression; the value of companionship — two are better than one.
chapters.5: Approach God with reverence; the emptiness of wealth; enjoy what God gives.
chapters.6: Wealth without the ability to enjoy it is meaningless.
chapters.7: Wisdom is valuable but has limits; no one is perfectly righteous.
chapters.8: The mystery of God's justice; obey the king; enjoy life despite uncertainty.
chapters.9: Death comes to all — enjoy life while you can; time and chance happen to everyone.
chapters.10: Practical wisdom about foolishness, rulers, and the consequences of laziness.
chapters.11: Be generous and take risks; rejoice in youth but remember judgment is coming.
chapters.12: Remember your Creator in your youth; the conclusion — fear God and keep His commandments.
